Humic acids
Here are some potential advantages of using humic acids for seed soaking:
1. Enhanced seed germination: Humic acids can help stimulate seed germination by breaking seed
dormancy and promoting the activation of enzymes involved in germination processes. Soaking
seeds in humic acids can potentially result in faster and more uniform germination rates.
2. Improved nutrient availability: Humic acids have the ability to chelate or bind with essential
nutrients, such as iron, zinc, and manganese, making them more available for plant uptake. By
soaking seeds in humic acids, the nutrients bound to these compounds can be released and
absorbed more efficiently by the emerging seedlings, promoting healthy growth.
3. Increased root development: Humic acids can stimulate root growth and development. Soaking
seeds in humic acids can help initiate root elongation, increase the number of root hairs, and
enhance lateral root branching. This can lead to improved nutrient and water uptake, as well as
better anchorage and overall plant vigor
4. Stress tolerance: Humic acids have been reported to enhance plant tolerance to
various abiotic stresses, including drought, salinity, and heavy metal toxicity. Soaking
seeds in humic acids can potentially prime the seedlings stress response mechanisms,
allowing them to better withstand adverse environmental conditions.
5. Microbial activity promotion: Humic acids can act as a food source and stimulant for
beneficial soil microorganisms. Soaking seeds in humic acids can promote the growth
and activity of beneficial bacteria and fungi in the rhizosphere, leading to improved
nutrient cycling, disease suppression, and overall soil health.
6. Seedling vigor and establishment: By providing a nutrient-rich and conducive
environment for seed germination, humic acid seed soaking can result in stronger and
more vigorous seedlings. This can lead to better establishment in the field, higher survival
rates, and improved early growth stages

Why Maxprolin?

  • Improves plant response to cold weather, frost, waterlogging, or drought;
  • Promotes seed germination, root hairs formation regulates water circulation in the plant;

Operating principle:

name: Azofix Plus
description:
Why Azofix Plus?

  • Organic fertilizer;
  • More efficient fixation of atmospheric nitrogen; up to 50 kg/ha of the active ingredient;
  • Higher seed germination energy;
  • The potential of plant genetic productivity is developed;
  • Better quality yield;
  • Promotes the biological activity of soils;
  • Improves soil structure and sorption, water and air regimes in the soil;
  • Can be used on organic farms.

Operating principle:

During the nitrogen fixation phase, nitrogen enters the soil from the atmosphere. The earth’s atmosphere contains large amounts of nitrogen gas (N2), but this nitrogen is “not available” to plants because plants cannot absorb gaseous nitrogen. In order for plants to absorb atmospheric nitrogen, the N2 must be transformed by nitrogen fixation. During fixation, atmospheric nitrogen is converted to a form that is available to plants. The Azofix Plus organic fertilizer bacteria derive energy from plants and in return, it fixes the nitrogen in a form that is accessible to the plant. The fixed nitrogen is transferred to other parts of the plant and used to form plant tissue, allowing the plant to grow and exploit its genetic productivity. Bacteria live freely in the soil and control the nitrogen fixation process.
